recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-39105 because the authoritative StructureDefinition source matches the Jira resolution and meeting decision.
issue_request: FHIR-39105 was a Published R5 FHIR-core/List change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked to align List.subject cardinality with Composition for lists of document bundles and the approved resolution was to change List.subject from 0..1 to 0..* and add a usage note warning about access-control and compartment challenges for Lists with multiple subjects.
initial_application: Commit a74c2edee9528723ae58535e3502101f87643347 applied the issue by pluralizing List.subject wording, changing max from 1 to *, and adding the requested multiple-subject security/access-control comment.
additional_context: FHIR-39104 is the directly related earlier List.subject issue that relaxed the target type to Reference(Any), enabling the ePI/MedicinalProductDefinition use case referenced in FHIR-39105 comments. FHIR Infrastructure WGM 202301 minutes record that a list-for extension alternative was considered but would not necessarily work, and that the WG accepted changing List.subject cardinality to 0..* with a 17-0-12 motion. Direct Zulip searches found no FHIR-39105 references.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current combined source has List active in source/fhir.ini and source/list/structuredefinition-List.xml already defines List.subject with max="*" and the requested usage note about multiple subjects affecting access control, security considerations, and patient compartments.
